packageRules.description: Backend (Go modules). gomodTidy runs `go mod tidy` after each bump so go.sum is reconciled in the same PR. A bare version bump updates only the changed module's go.sum hashes; indirect-dep additions/removals it leaves behind would otherwise fail `go mod download` / `go mod verify` in CI and block auto-merge. postUpdateOptions is a normal repo-config option (NOT the self-hosted-only postUpgradeTasks command allowlist), so it works on the hosted Mend app.

Frontend (npm / pnpm). Override rangeStrategy to 'replace' so engines constraints (e.g. node >=24.0.0 <25.0.0) and caret ranges are only rewritten when the new version no longer satisfies them; the top-level 'bump' default would otherwise churn lower bounds on every patch.

Landing page (site/). It is its own pnpm workspace with its own lockfile and deploy cadence (landing.yml publishes site/dist to gh-pages), so it gets its own group/scope/labels instead of riding the catch-all 'frontend dependencies' rule above. Renovate has no dedicated pnpm manager: the npm manager handles pnpm, pnpm-lock.yaml and pnpm-workspace.yaml, so matchManagers stays 'npm' and matchFileNames scopes the rule to site/. Placed before the pnpm-toolchain rule below so site/package.json's 'packageManager' pnpm pin still groups into 'pnpm toolchain'. rangeStrategy 'replace' mirrors the frontend rule.

Hold TypeScript on the latest 6.x. typescript@7 is the native Go port: its package exports map resolves '.' to lib/version.cjs and it no longer ships lib/typescript.js. Next.js probes for exactly that file in dist/lib/verify-typescript-setup.js to detect TypeScript, so `next build` aborts with 'you do not have the required package(s) installed' even though `tsc --noEmit` passes. That breaks the frontend build, the Playwright webServer and the Vercel deploy at once. allowedVersions caps how far an upgrade may go without freezing the dependency, so 6.x releases keep flowing through the normal minor/patch automerge path while 7.x is filtered out. It carries no matchUpdateTypes because Renovate rejects that combination in a single rule. Lift this cap once Next.js supports the native compiler for a non-preview `typescript` dependency (it currently only special-cases @typescript/native-preview).

Toolchain pins managed by mise (mise.toml, backend/mise.toml). Covers Go, Node, pnpm, supabase CLI, python, pipx, ansible-core, rust, mprocs. Every tool pin lives in a mise.toml: the repo dropped the legacy .tool-versions format, which Renovate routed through its asdf manager and parsed only partially — supabase, pipx and pipx:ansible-core were never detected there.

Bundle the Go toolchain pin in backend/mise.toml with the 'go' directive in backend/go.mod into a single PR, so they cannot drift apart between CI (mise-action, run with working_directory: backend) and the module graph.
Bundle the pnpm pin in mise.toml with the packageManager fields into one PR: Vercel reads packageManager (no mise there), CI reads mise.toml, and the two must not drift.

Hold pnpm at 11.x: Vercel cannot run pnpm 12. Since v12 the npm package ships `pnpm.exe` as a text placeholder that a preinstall script swaps for the real native binary, and Vercel installs the packageManager version without running lifecycle scripts, so the shell execs the placeholder and `pnpm install` fails. Only Vercel is affected — mise installs pnpm from release binaries, so local dev and CI stay green. Lift once Vercel supports pnpm 12.
Auto-merge minor and patch updates after CI passes

GitHub Actions require human review for any update. Actions execute in CI with secrets in scope, so a compromised maintainer publishing a malicious patch would otherwise auto-merge. CVE-flagged updates already bypass automerge via vulnerabilityAlerts; this rule extends that to all GHA updates regardless of severity flag.

Toolchain (mise) bumps require human review. Runtime version changes (Go, Node, pnpm, supabase CLI) can shift build/test behavior even on patch releases and propagate into CI via mise.toml, so a bad bump can break every workflow at once.
Pin Go toolchain bumps for manual review
